stages.title: Mapping Your Target
stages.description: Before finding bugs in an application, first understand what it is about.
topics: What is the goal of this app
Target user category - is it for public usage or for internal usage
Use all functions in the app with proxy configured to log requests history
What is the technology used in backend/frontend/web server/operating system
Does it use a framework for client side or not?
Quick check on headers - are there weird headers? Is there caching system? Can headers help fingerprint app
Check cookies, auth headers, local storage
Quick check on console - are there errors?
What caught your eyes while exploring you want to focus on later?

stages.title: Common Server-Side Vulnerabilities
stages.description: Learn to identify and exploit common server-side web application vulnerabilities. To ensure you understand a vulnerability, ask yourself - what is it, what is the root cause, how to exploit, mitigation.

SQL Injection: In-Band SQL Injection (Union and Error Based)
RCE From SQL Injection Root Cause
Writing Your Own Script to Exploit the Bug
Bonus: Try Exploit the Bug in MySQL/Oracle/SQLite - What is the Difference
Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI): What is Template Engines and How Does it Work?
Write Simple Python App with Jinja2
Does Same Concept Apply for Smarty PHP?
Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF): How to Identify SSRF From Client Side Request
File Upload Attacks: What Environment Unrestricted File Upload Can Lead to RCE
Broken Access Control: How Does Access Control Applied in Web Apps
Insecure Deserialization: What are Common Vulnerable Functions in Languages
XML Attacks: Understand Root Cause of XML Attacks
Authentication Attacks: Host Header Injection in Forget Password Link
Race Condition: Race Condition Example in File Upload
Race Conditions Example in Bypassing Server-Side Restrictions
Vulnerable and Outdated Components: Identify Outdated Components Used by Backend
How to Search for CVEs and Exploits Online
API Attacks: RESTful APIs vs SOAP vs GraphQL
How to Interact with APIs Without Web App
Directory Traversal Attacks: LFI vs RFI vs LFD in PHP
Improper Session Handling: Inactive Sessions Remain Valid After Logout
Logic Bugs: Logic bugs depend on application business itself
Check multi-step process - can you drop one step and continue or does it check sequence?
Check what data inputs can cause errors - does it have to be a positive number?
HTTP Request Smuggling: How Backend and Frontend Servers Process HTTP Requests Differently
CL.TE Request Smuggling (Front-end uses Content-Length, Back-end uses Transfer-Encoding)
TE.CL Request Smuggling (Front-end uses Transfer-Encoding, Back-end uses Content-Length)

stages.title: Introduction to OSINT
stages.description: Understand the fundamentals of Open Source Intelligence, including its types, process, and applications.

About OSINT: Open Source Intelligence (OSINT) involves gathering information from publicly available sources
Active vs Passive Information Gathering: Scanning a host or interacting with a human to get information is active info gathering
Getting information without the target knowing is passive, most commonly from public resources
OSINT Process: Identify the data you have first

Specialized Search.title: GrayHatWarfare
Specialized Search.description: Search engine for open cloud storage buckets

Google Dorks: Advanced search techniques to get exact information using specific operators

What is GEOINT About: Goal: Find location from an image
Metadata can reveal info about place, camera model, etc.
Buildings, roads, signs, environment features can reveal info about place

Sock Puppets: Understanding fake accounts used for intelligence gathering
Advanced Search in Social Media: Searching by username and username combinations

Getting Information About an Image: Checking sources (social media, CCTV, newspaper, drone, satellite)

Whois Lookup: Perform Whois lookup to gather domain registration information such as owner, registrar, and creation date
Shodan Search: Use Shodan to search for internet-connected devices and services associated with the target domain
Subdomain Enumeration: Discover subdomains using tools like Subfinder, Sublist3r, and verify active ones with httpx
ASN-based Domain Discovery: Find ASN numbers for the target and search for other domains using the same ASN
Favicon-based Search: Search for domains using favicon hashes or images to find related websites
Footer Data Search: Use Google dorks to search for domains based on common footer information like copyright notices
Acquired Companies Check: Research if the target company has acquired other companies and check their domains

How Does Blockchain Work: Blockchain is a distributed ledger technology that records transactions across a network
Each transaction is permanently recorded and publicly accessible
Blockchain intelligence helps trace cryptocurrency transactions and identify wallet owners
What is a Wallet: A wallet is a digital address that holds cryptocurrency
Wallets can be identified by their unique public addresses
Analyzing wallet activity can reveal transaction patterns and connections
What is a Transaction Number: Transaction hash (TxID) is a unique identifier for each blockchain transaction
Allows tracking of funds from sender to receiver
Can reveal transaction amount, timestamp, and involved addresses

Understanding APT Groups: Advanced Persistent Threats (APTs) are sophisticated, organized cyber threat actors
Often state-sponsored or well-funded criminal organizations
Understanding APT tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) helps in threat intelligence
